description: PACKAGING: the capstone orchestrator ships with the starter and is executable — the 14-step workflow is a runnable artifact, not a slideshow
command: [ -x scripts/capstone-triage.sh ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: TRIAGE DISCIPLINE: the INC-006 compound incident ticket exists — you validate the incident before you touch anything
command: [ -f incidents/INC-006-campaign-capstone.md ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: TRIAGE DISCIPLINE (lock before investigate): acquiring the triage lock for INC-006 succeeds, and a concurrent second acquire for the same correlation id is rejected — exactly one loop owns the incident
command: scripts/triage-lock.sh --release --cid m19-check >/dev/null 2>&1; scripts/triage-lock.sh --acquire --cid m19-check >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! scripts/triage-lock.sh --acquire --cid m19-check >/dev/null 2>&1 && { scripts/triage-lock.sh --release --cid m19-check >/dev/null 2>&1; echo locked; } || echo open

description: TRIAGE DISCIPLINE: Phase 1 gate passes — incident locked, evidence present, hypotheses formed, tracks delegated
command: scripts/capstone-triage.sh reset >/dev/null 2>&1; scripts/capstone-triage.sh phase1 --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: EVIDENCE QUALITY: the three capstone hypotheses each carry their OWN sources (>=1) — structured, multi-source evidence, not one guess echoed three times
command: jq -e 'length==3 and (all(.[]; (.sources|length)>=1 and .derived_from==null))' fixtures/capstone/hypotheses.json >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: EVIDENCE QUALITY: independent tracks converge on one root cause — real corroboration, verified by the synthesizer rather than asserted
command: scripts/synthesize-hypotheses.sh fixtures/capstone/hypotheses.json 2>/dev/null | awk -F= '/^verdict=/{print $2}'

description: EVIDENCE QUALITY (anti-consensus-theater): a packet that derives from a peer instead of its own evidence is rejected — agreement built on anchoring is worth nothing
command: jq '[.[0], (.[1] + {derived_from:"application-retry", sources:[]})]' fixtures/capstone/hypotheses.json | scripts/synthesize-hypotheses.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 4 ] && echo rejected || echo accepted

description: ROLE ADHERENCE: the sre-investigator is a reader — write authority is structurally absent, so the investigator can query but never edit
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh sre-investigator write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo readonly || echo writer

description: ROLE ADHERENCE: the change-reviewer inspects but never modifies — an independent reviewer with write authority is not independent
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh change-reviewer write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo readonly || echo writer

description: ROLE ADHERENCE: the iac-engineer IS a writer — authoring HCL is inside its role, so the boundary is scoped, not blanket-deny
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh iac-engineer write >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo writer || echo readonly

description: ROLE ADHERENCE: all seven governed-team role bundles resolve in the authority matrix — the full team the capstone operates with
command: for r in sre-investigator iac-engineer platform-engineer security-reviewer finops-analyst mlops-engineer change-reviewer; do grep -q "^  $r:" contracts/authority-matrix.yaml || { echo missing; exit 0; }; done; echo pass

description: ROLE ADHERENCE: Phase 2 gate passes — the parallel tracks investigate independently and reconcile on one root cause
command: scripts/capstone-triage.sh phase2 --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: INFRASTRUCTURE JUDGMENT: the review pipeline BLOCKS the dangerous prod plan (open 0.0.0.0/0 security groups) — the agent proposes, the chain rejects
command: scripts/change-pipeline.sh infra/fixtures/plan-wide-network.json --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: INFRASTRUCTURE JUDGMENT: the security stage independently flags the exposure — the block is a reasoned objection, not a coin flip
command: scripts/tf-security-scan.sh infra/fixtures/plan-wide-network.json --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: INFRASTRUCTURE JUDGMENT: the oversize plan fixture carries the db.r6g.4xlarge the incident names — the FinOps-scale concern is real and inspectable
command: jq -e '[.resource_changes[].change.after.instance_class?]|any(.=="db.r6g.4xlarge")' infra/fixtures/plan-oversize.json >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: REPAIR SAFETY: the PreToolUse change gate denies a direct `terraform apply` on production — repairs go proposal -> review -> gate, never direct apply
command: printf '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"terraform apply -auto-approve -chdir=infra/environments/production"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo denied || echo allowed

description: REPAIR SAFETY: the same gate ALLOWS a read-only `terraform plan` — the boundary blocks the irreversible action, not the investigation
command: printf '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"terraform plan -chdir=infra/environments/production"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] && echo allowed || echo denied

description: REPAIR SAFETY: Phase 3 gate passes — dangerous plan blocked by the review chain and write authority scoped to writers only
command: scripts/capstone-triage.sh phase3 --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: REPAIR SAFETY (deploy & verify): a healthy canary is promoted — the safe release ships only after its SLOs verify
command: scripts/canary-verify.sh fixtures/canary/canary-healthy.json --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: REPAIR SAFETY (deploy & verify): a degraded canary is rolled back — the verify step catches the bad deploy before it takes the fleet
command: scripts/canary-verify.sh fixtures/canary/canary-unhealthy.json --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: REPAIR SAFETY: Phase 4 gate passes — healthy canary promoted, degraded canary rolled back
command: scripts/capstone-triage.sh phase4 --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: POST-INCIDENT EVALUATION: the capstone run scores composite PASS on all five evaluation dimensions — a right outcome reached by right reasoning
command: scripts/eval-score.sh fixtures/capstone/run-capstone.json --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: POST-INCIDENT EVALUATION: the regression gate passes the capstone run and would fail the build on a degraded one — quality is code with a CI gate
command: scripts/regression-gate.sh fixtures/capstone/run-capstone.json --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: CAPSTONE END-TO-END: running all four phase gates in order completes the 14-step workflow with no gate skipped or failed
command: scripts/capstone-triage.sh reset >/dev/null 2>&1; scripts/capstone-triage.sh all --field verdict 2>/dev/null | tail -1

description: PART I: the four investigation tracks in agentops/capstone/tracks/ were produced by your subagents, each with derived_from null — not read from fixtures/capstone/
command: ls agentops/capstone/tracks/*.json >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo none; exit 0; }; n=$(ls agentops/capstone/tracks/*.json | wc -l | tr -d ' '); jq -e -s '[.[] | .derived_from] | all(. == null)' agentops/capstone/tracks/*.json >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$n" -ge 3 ] && echo independent || echo derivative

description: NANO PROJECT: you named the agent you built in agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt — the grader follows your declaration, whichever option you chose
command: [ -s agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt ] && echo declared || echo undeclared

description: NANO PROJECT: the skill exists and is not one of the seven that shipped with the course — this one is yours
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; for s in incident-triage k8s-diagnose release-check service-health service-restart terraform-plan-review terraform-style; do [ "$N" = "$s" ] && { echo shipped; exit 0; }; done; [ -f .claude/skills/$N/SKILL.md ] && echo new || echo missing

description: NANO PROJECT: the skill separates a deterministic collection zone from a reasoning zone and carries a NEVER DO list
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; S=.claude/skills/$N/SKILL.md; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qi "deterministic" $S && grep -qi "reasoning" $S && grep -qi "never" $S && echo structured || echo unstructured

description: NANO PROJECT: a scoped role ships alongside the skill — the tool bundle is what makes the dangerous action structurally impossible
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; [ -f .claude/agents/$N.md ] && echo present || echo missing

description: NANO PROJECT: the role is wired into contracts/authority-matrix.yaml — a role outside the matrix is undeclared authority
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; grep -q "$N" contracts/authority-matrix.yaml && echo wired || echo unwired

description: NANO PROJECT: role-authority-check refuses a write for your role — the agent you shipped cannot mutate what it inspects
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; scripts/role-authority-check.sh "$N" write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -ne 0 ] && echo blocked || echo writable

description: NANO PROJECT: it ships — a row in starter/MANIFEST.md and a stage entry in starter/adoption-ladder.yaml with its own trust gate
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; grep -q "$N" starter/MANIFEST.md && grep -q "$N" starter/adoption-ladder.yaml && echo shipped || echo unpackaged

description: NANO PROJECT: starter/CHANGELOG.md records the addition — a starter that changes without a changelog entry cannot be rolled back deliberately
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; grep -q "$N" starter/CHANGELOG.md && echo recorded || echo silent

description: NANO PROJECT: the packet your agent produced passes an existing validator — output nothing else can read is not a handoff
command: N=$(head -1 agentops/capstone/nano-project.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d "[:space:]"); [ -n "$N" ] || { echo undeclared; exit 0; }; F=agentops/capstone/$N-packet.json; [ -f $F ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; scripts/evidence-validate.sh $F >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo valid || echo invalid

description: NANO PROJECT: you broke it on purpose and captured the finding — agentops/capstone/break-it.md names what the agent caught
command: [ -s agentops/capstone/break-it.md ] && echo captured || echo missing

description: NANO PROJECT: agentops/capstone/defense.md answers all six questions, including what it cannot do and what would make you turn it off
command: F=agentops/capstone/defense.md; [ -f $F ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; n=$(grep -c '^##' $F); [ "$n" -ge 6 ] && echo defended || echo incomplete
